title: Redcliffe — declared route and canonical identity contract
purpose: Reviewable structural scope only. Shared national QA is linked with its actual limits; official source and per-place browser review remain distinct.
coverageNotes: Current office is independently sourced from the Parliament’s current roster, published as at 23 September 2026 and retrieved 17 October 2026. Official public profile identity/district/party is separately reconciled; it is not inferred from the 2024 winner.
Historical election records use the boundaries applying at each event. The 2026 redistributed boundaries take effect for the 2028 general election; earlier by-elections use the existing boundaries.

All previous ballot contestants are retained, including unsuccessful candidates. Historical personal/campaign websites are not assumed to remain available; every contestant has the original ECQ result record.

The ECQ public Final archive contains declared candidates and official count rounds while retaining district final=NO flags. This adapter preserves that flag and labels the data as a declared archived official count rather than rewriting the source flag.
No local Twinkles or inferred resident views are created.
23 October review reconciled aggregate party totals and all member surnames/districts to the official 20 October PDF. This text-presence check is not a fresh individual-profile audit.
Declared scope is this place route, visible implementation date, breadcrumbs, choices and canonical place identity/boundary pins only.
This manifest does not claim a complete civic journey, current source/legal correctness, full biographies or full historical contestant coverage.
Geometry, people, candidate measures and timing received only the actual checks recorded in the linked national report; their missing coverage remains explicit there.

Browser evidence is a shared-renderer smoke review of its recorded fixtures and viewport/device conditions. It does not establish full per-place source, geometry, mobile, accessibility or browser review.
No new Twinkles were authored; grassroots implementation remains open. A structural PASS is not a national completeness claim.
